checksums.name: candidate_header_word_0x0000
checksums.formula_detail: No checksum routine (sum/XOR/CRC loop) exists in ghidra/decompiled.c (58 functions). Only integrity gate is FUN_08000588 first-dword compare *piVar1 != _DAT_08000664 (literal-pool value unresolved). Python tests on cap-01: sum8/sum16/sum32/xor8/crc32/crc16-Modbus over [0,0x1768),[4,0x1768),[4,0x1818) all != 0x1ad0c863 and != its halves; payload after offset 4 is all 0x00 so any plain sum/XOR over payload = 0x0. Header is therefore more likely a magic/ID word than a payload checksum, but equality to the code constant cannot be proven without literal-pool values.

io_driver_functions.notes: SRAM writer/verify entry (MMIO seed, no recovered callers, jumptable dispatch). Calls FUN_08016078, func_0x08016eb4(RAM_base,0x0E000000,len from _DAT_08000584), func_0x08016f24(RAM_base,0x0E000000,len) verify, FUN_080160c4. Pre-write struct field stores at offsets derived from literal pool incl +0x3C/+0x10C relative fields.

SRAM reader/validator entry. func_0x08016e50(0x0E000000,RAM_base,len) reads SRAM to RAM; then if *RAM_base != _DAT_08000664, ORs a mask over 0x29 halfwords at two offsets (+_DAT_08000674/+_DAT_08000678) - invalid-save sanitisation. No recovered callers.

Byte-copy SRAM write loop: while(len-- != -1) *dst++=*src++; sets WAITCNT-related *_DAT_08016eec & mask |3 before copy. Direct SRAM at 0x0E000000, no Flash 0x5555/0x2AAA sequence, no EEPROM DMA3 0x040000D4.
Wrapper: stack-canary/copy guard then func_0x08016fcc(SRAM,RAM,len,guard) - Nintendo-style SRAM read/verify helper (body of 0x08016fcc not recovered, jumptable only).
Same shape as 0x08016e50; used after write in 0x08000488 as verify/read-back via func_0x08016fcc.
Unrecovered jumptable stub in decompilation; inferred common SRAM transfer core from call sites only - CONFIRMED_STATIC for existence, HYPOTHESIS for exact semantics.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If header is the magic checked by 0x08000588, save rejected/sanitised (0x29-halfword OR-mask path) - game boots as new/blank or clears progress. If no effect, header is not (sole) validity gate.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: No checksum repair known/needed (no checksum proven); observe which phrase/score/setting changes in UI/RAM to subdivide the zero payload. Rejection on load would reveal a hidden checksum - then locate it.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Distinguishes secondary struct vs tail: loss of a specific setting/progress implicates this span; no effect suggests padding/unused.
No gameplay change expected if gap is unwritten; a change would show the reader consumes a longer contiguous struct than the writer normally flushes.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Tests for hidden integrity beyond header: silent acceptance = no payload checksum; rejection = search decompiled code for a checksum missed due to jumptable stubs (0x08016fcc).

open_questions: Literal-pool values (_DAT_08000538 base, _DAT_08000584 length, _DAT_08000664 expected header, all field offsets) are unresolved in the trace-guided decompilation, so RAM mirror addresses, exact write length(s), and header==magic equality cannot be proven from this workspace.

No checksum algorithm was found and all standard checksums were rejected against the samples; is there integrity inside the unrecovered 0x08016fcc jumptable stub, or is the first-dword compare the only gate?
What is the 12-byte span at 0x180C-0x1817 and the 164-byte gap before it - second struct, second slot, or sparse fields of one struct?
How is the 5988-byte zero payload subdivided (650 phrase states, scores, settings)? Requires a progressed (non-zero) save or the fuzzing sweep; both corpus saves are blank/initialised only.
Who calls 0x08000488/0x08000588? Callgraph shows no callers (jumptable/indirect dispatch); trigger contexts (boot, phrase completion, settings change) are unknown.
Only 2 of the 6 corpus files described in PACKET.md metadata are present in saves/ (2 .sav on disk); additional progressed states would raise confidence.
